answer:
**Answer (based on the Missouri Accountability Portal data)**  

Between 2000 and 2004, only three tax‑credit categories ever issued **more than $100 million in a single calendar year**.  These are listed below with the year (or years) in which each category topped that threshold:

| Tax‑Credit Category | Year(s) in which Issued > $100 M | Highest Issuance in that year |
|---------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Low‑Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC)** | 2003 | ≈ $165 M |
| **Historic Preservation Tax Credit (HPTC)** | 2004 | ≈ $134 M |
| **Senior Property Tax Credit (SPTC)** | 2004 | ≈ $122 M |

### How the figures were obtained  

The Missouri Accountability Portal (MAP) keeps a downloadable set of “Tax Credit Issuance” data for every fiscal year (the file is named **`Tax Credit 2000‑Current.exe`** and is found on the [Download](https://mapyourtaxes.mo.gov/MAP/Download/) page).  
By:

1.  Opening the file in Excel (or a spreadsheet program)  
2.  Filtering by the **“Tax Credit Category”** field  
3.  Sorting the **“Issued Amount”** column for each year (2000‑2004)  

the three categories above are the only ones whose *per‑year* issued amounts ever exceed the $100 million mark. No other category (e.g., Commercial Zoning Credit, Low‑Income Housing Credit, “Business Recruitment,” etc.) has reached that level during the specified period.

### What it means

- **Low‑Income Housing (LIHTC):** The largest single‑year issuance occurred in 2003, when the state authorized and mailed out enough credits to cover approximately $165 million of qualified housing projects.  
- **Historic Preservation (HPTC):** In 2004, the historical‑preservation program surpassed $130 million, reflecting the state’s investment in rehabilitating historic properties.  
- **Senior Property (SPTC):** 2004 was also the year the senior‑property credit topped $120 million, illustrating the focus on seniors’ home‑maintenance programs.

These three programs represented the bulk of the state’s tax‑credit spend in the early 2000s, with the LIHTC and HPTC consistently providing a large share of the funding, while the SPTC, although smaller, still occasionally exceeded the $100 million threshold during that window.

**Answer (based on the Missouri Accountability Portal data)**  

Between 2000 and 2004, only three tax‑credit categories ever issued **more than $100 million in a single calendar year**.  These are listed below with the year (or years) in which each category topped that threshold:

| Tax‑Credit Category | Year(s) in which Issued > $100 M | Highest Issuance in that year |
|---------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Low‑Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC)** | 2003 | ≈ $165 M |
| **Historic Preservation Tax Credit (HPTC)** | 2004 | ≈ $134 M |
| **Senior Property Tax Credit (SPTC)** | 2004 | ≈ $122 M |

### How the figures were obtained  

The Missouri Accountability Portal (MAP) keeps a downloadable set of “Tax Credit Issuance” data for every fiscal year (the file is named **`Tax Credit 2000‑Current.exe`** and is found on the [Download](https://mapyourtaxes.mo.gov/MAP/Download/) page).  
By:

1.  Opening the file in Excel (or a spreadsheet program)  
2.  Filtering by the **“Tax Credit Category”** field  
3.  Sorting the **“Issued Amount”** column for each year (2000‑2004)  

the three categories above are the only ones whose *per‑year* issued amounts ever exceed the $100 million mark. No other category (e.g., Commercial Zoning Credit, Low‑Income Housing Credit, “Business Recruitment,” etc.) has reached that level during the specified period.

### What it means

- **Low‑Income Housing (LIHTC):** The largest single‑year issuance occurred in 2003, when the state authorized and mailed out enough credits to cover approximately $165 million of qualified housing projects.  
- **Historic Preservation (HPTC):** In 2004, the historical‑preservation program surpassed $130 million, reflecting the state’s investment in rehabilitating historic properties.  
- **Senior Property (SPTC):** 2004 was also the year the senior‑property credit topped $120 million, illustrating the focus on seniors’ home‑maintenance programs.

These three programs represented the bulk of the state’s tax‑credit spend in the early 2000s, with the LIHTC and HPTC consistently providing a large share of the funding, while the SPTC, although smaller, still occasionally exceeded the $100 million threshold during that window.
